NOT ALREADY HANDLED, AND THE HOUSE ALREADY KNOWS THE RULE. src/notes.js:1250 does exactly this — `say(`Open. ${note.title.replace(/[.?!]+$/, "")}. Open on the desk.`)`. SEVERITY, corrected down to the mild end of defect. Nothing untrue is asserted, so it is not misleading, and nothing fails to work, so it is not blocking. FIX JUDGED. The proposed regex is correct against the real source and matches line 1250's existing pattern, so it is defensible as written. Two things it gets slightly wrong, corrected in sharpenedFix: (1) `[.!?]+$` flattens a question into a statement — no shipped body ends in `?` or `!`, but `makeNote` is also the live-capture path, so a note typed as "Can we move the ceremony?" would be named "Can we move the ceremony. Typed. Just now. Still to decide.", losing the interrogative for exactly the user the label exists for; (2) the identical expression appears again 16 lines down in `data-full` on `.idxText` (src/notes.js:1961), and hoisting a stripped `head` into that would silently amputate the terminal stop from the row's full text. Conditional joining fixes both risks and is no longer.
confirmed.sharpenedFix:
In src/notes.js, replace the non-crossed arm of the `name` ternary (lines 1940-1945) with a conditional join rather than a strip, and leave the crossed arm alone:

  const head = `${note.title} ${note.rest || ""}`.trim();
  const name = crossed
    ? `${note.task}. In Tasks, ${note.lane}. Sent to Tasks ${when}. The note it came from stayed in Notes.`
    : `${head}${/[.!?…]$/.test(head) ? "" : "."} ${src.label}. ${note.when}.${note.pending ? " Still to decide." : note.sent ? " In Tasks." : " Kept."}`;

This removes the doubled stop on all fourteen rows, keeps a live-captured question or exclamation intact instead of turning it into a statement, and adds the missing stop for a capture that has no terminal punctuation at all — which the seat's version would also have handled, but only by accident of the head already ending clean. Widen the test to /[.!?…][”"’')\]]*$/ if you want a body ending in a closing quote after the stop to join cleanly too.

Do not reuse `head` for the `data-full` attribute on `.idxText` (src/notes.js:1961) — that string is the row's visible full text and must keep its terminal stop. Write the regex to the file with an editor, not through a shell; the character class contains `!` and `$` and the ellipsis is a literal U+2026.

confirmed.problem: The card's move menu is positioned with the inline style `left:8px;top:-250px` — a constant — at every card, in every lane, at 390, 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, with a fine pointer and with a coarse one. I measured the rect as [8,−250,188,213] in all twelve combinations I drove. The menu is entirely above the top of the viewport and never visible. The cause is at src/tasks.js:2041: `const host = window.__SUITE.host("tasks")` returns DIV.app, which the suite shell sets to `display: contents`, so `host.getBoundingClientRect()` is all zeros; `top = Math.min(box.bottom - frame.top + 6, frame.height - 250)` therefore always picks `0 - 250`. The menu's actual offset parent is `.floor`, not the host, so the origin is wrong twice over. Meanwhile `.menuVeil` renders at the full viewport size and is transparent, so the board looks untouched and the person's next click is eaten dismissing an invisible menu.
confirmed.consequence: Orla presses the only control on a card labelled "Move this task" and absolutely nothing happens on screen — twice, because the veil swallows her second press too. On her phone this is not one route of three: drag is a pointer gesture she cannot make and Space-carry needs a keyboard, so the source's own comment calls this menu "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take". On a phone the board's primary action is unreachable. Keyboard focus does enter the menu, so a screen-reader user operates a control nobody can see.
confirmed.fix: In the `menu` branch of src/tasks.js (~2038–2046) stop measuring the suite host. Take the origin from the menu's real offset parent and the clamp from the viewport: `const frame = document.querySelector('.floor').getBoundingClientRect(); let top = box.bottom - frame.top + 6; let left = Math.min(box.left - frame.left, innerWidth - frame.left - 200); if (box.bottom + 219 > innerHeight) top = box.top - frame.top - 219;` then `menuAt = 'left:' + Math.max(8, Math.round(left)) + 'px;top:' + Math.round(top) + 'px'`. Never clamp against a rect that can be zero — a `display: contents` ancestor must not be able to decide where a popover lands.
confirmed.assertion: For every lane's first card, at 390×844 (touch), 768×1024, 1280×900, 1440×960 and 1920×1000: open the menu from `.cardDots`, then assert `.cardMenu`'s rect is fully inside the viewport (top ≥ 0, bottom ≤ innerHeight, left ≥ 0, right ≤ innerWidth), that `document.elementFromPoint` at its centre is inside `.cardMenu`, and that the rect for a card low in a lane differs from the rect for a card at the top of that lane.
confirmed.verdict:
CONFIRMED, and every number in it is exact. Driven in Chromium against file:///C:/.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board at 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, with a fine pointer and with a coarse/touch context, clicking .cardDots on the first, middle and last card in each: the style attribute is literally `left:8px;top:-250px` and the rect is [8,-250,188,213] in all of them. The menu's bottom edge is at -37; it is entirely above the viewport at every card, in every lane, at every width.

The diagnosis is right down to the element. `window.__SUITE.host("tasks")` is `hostOf()` in src/app.js:86-88, which returns `[data-app="tasks"]`, i.e. DIV.app, and src/shell.css:93 sets `.app { display: contents; }`. I measured `host.getBoundingClientRect()` at runtime: [0,0,0,0] at all five widths. So at src/tasks.js:2044-2045 `top = Math.min(box.bottom - 0 + 6, 0 - 250)` always resolves to -250 and `left = Math.min(box.left, -200)` is floored to 8 by the Math.max. The seat is also right that the origin is wrong twice over: I read `menu.offsetParent` and it is DIV.floor, never the host.

The consequences are as described. `.menuVeil` measures [0,0,390,844] / [0,0,1440,960] with `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0)`, and `document.elementFromPoint(centre)` returns DIV.menuVeil — the board looks untouched and the next click is eaten. The aria-live region is empty, so nothing is announced either.

Blocking is the correct class, not overstated. The code's own comment at src/tasks.css:891-892 and src/tasks.js:800-802 says this menu is "the one route to moving a card that a mouse, a finger and a keyboard can all take… on a touch screen there was no way at all to move a card" — and at ≤720 src/tasks.css:1465 makes .cardDots permanently visible, so on Orla's phone this is the only advertised way to move a card and it does nothing visible. The product does not do what it says.

Not a restatement of either gate: I grepped interaction-check.mjs for cardMenu / cardDots / menuVeil / moveto and there is not one assertion. It cannot be — `cardMenu()` returns "" unless `menuFor` is set, and no gated state sets it, so the menu is not in the DOM in any shot or any checked state. This is precisely what automation cannot see. Not in the 34 already-fixed list, not in the refuted list, not a lessons.md class.

I also verified the proposed fix's premises rather than taking them on trust, because the fix hardcodes `.floor`: there is exactly one `.floor` in _gate-suite.html, _gate-tasks.html AND master.html (so tasks.js does not throw when run standalone); its computed border is 0px on all sides, so its border box and padding box share an origin and getBoundingClientRect is the right rect for an absolutely-positioned child; `position: relative`, `overflow: visible`, scrollTop/scrollLeft 0 with scrollHeight === clientHeight, so no scroll offset to correct for; and no ancestor of the host carries a transform, filter, perspective or paint containment. The fix's own geometry checks out: I replayed its formula against every .cardDots box at all five widths and every menu that corresponds to an actually-clickable card lands fully inside the viewport. The only "failures" in the replay are cards that are themselves off-screen (below the tray fold at 390, or in a lane scrolled off to the right at box.left 1469), which you cannot click without first scrolling them in.

So: correct problem, correct diagnosis, correct severity, and a fix whose direction and origin are verified sound. It is confirmed. Two numbers in it are soft rather than wrong, and it is missing two clamps — sharpened below.

1. The mouse route that already works. A reader scrolled to the sheet's bottom stop sees all three rows today (measured: 1440×960 scrollTop 249 = max, rows 741–859 inside a sheet ending at 942). The fix must stay a no-op there. Re-measure the click-at-bottom route at 1440, 1920, 1280, 768 and 390 and confirm scrollTop is unchanged to the pixel.
